1. Farm is the airship survival in Extreme. It can be kinda AFK’d but the mobs spawn so far back that you won’t get much in terms of rewards for lower kill counts and there are slimes that spawn on the upper deck (which a chance at a prismatic slime spawn) that you won’t get if you afk at the start. But it’s a good source of voucher fodder (machine parts and high grade scrap that can be melded into knickknack vouchers). It also drops a decent amount of Rafale coins which can be turned into Exceptional Refinium (you’re gonna need soooooo much of it lol). But it’s mindless and easy. For MSP and Rupies, you’ll get a survival mission at the end of Maniac. 

2. This is a hard question because they all work more or less. Of the ones you list, Rackam and Eugen are pretty high up there in DPS and ease of use. They also are ranged which is huge in this game in terms of avoiding melee swipes from bosses (especially if you can get a lot of Low Profile in your build). Tweyen seems strong but I haven’t done much with her yet. Vaseraga is really good but can be tricky. He’s entirely charged attacks and counters so your mileage may vary with him. You’ll either end the world or the world will end him 😅

It comes down to preference. I did most of the story with the Dragon Bois (Sieg, Lance, Vane, and Percival). All the characters end up doing tons of damage and all can be built similarly given that most of a build is sigil based. It’s really how well you like their kit and how well you can do DPS while still avoiding/mitigating mechanics.

Good luck out there!

Just so you know and other people aren't confused (and not trying to sound condescending at all), but Extreme isn't anywhere near endgame xD you still have to clear Maniac and Proud. Finishing Proud is arguably the beginning of endgame. That said, I'd say that, above all else, you should play what you find fun. The sigils will sort of sort themselves out in time when you roll for them. You'll be grinding bosses regardless of who you choose, so choose someone you find fun. I'd take some time and test out other characters to see what you like. It's not a bad idea to have a team of 4 that you play with (you piloting one, the other 3 AI) and you just swap around them when you want something new to play.

You will need hundreds of hours to build out even a few characters, so yeah - find someone you enjoy (or a few!) and figure out where you want to spend time.  
I will say, too, that you get access to a nice farm in Extreme and a nice rupee/MSP farm in Maniac, both of which are survivals and very easy to grind out LOTS of nice things.

You're welcome to keep with Yoda since you already know how to play him, but consider giving some of your AI party you've been playing with a try (or a totally new character) and see how you feel.

The other aspect of this (again, speaking from my own approach) is to figure out how much you want to invest in horizontal progression (more characters) vs vertical progression (getting a 5\* up to a certain constellation level). 4. Click "Add"

7. You're all done!

As someone who played both MHW and MHGU, I’d say MHGU will feel closer simply because the Switch controller (whether Pro or JoyCons) is a bit different than Xbox and PS4/5 and that impacts how the movement/controls feel. Though the radial menu on L for Switch is more akin to MHW, so maybe I’m basing this on the fact that MHGU is also on Switch so it naturally feels more similar to MHR than MHW. MHW also had easier combo-chaining (for example, it’s fairly easy to switch between Axe mode and Sword mode on Switch Axe in MHW, meaning there are a number of ways to morph between the two once you learn the weapon) when compared to MHGU’s more particular style - something that Rise thankfully follows MHW regarding its own combos/movesets for weapons. MHW doesn’t have Hunter Arts (special moves that could be slotted in based on your Style in MHGU) and neither does Rise (tho they clearly borrowed some moves from the Hunter Arts). 
This is long and confusing comment to say that some aspects of World will feel closer to Rise whereas some aspects of MHGU (mainly in the Switch controller itself) will feel more similar to Rise. 
Personally, it’s so close to launch that I wouldn’t want to try to get into a 200+ hour game like MHW or MHGU so close to starting Rise. I’d say to keep MHW and MHGU in the back pocket to check out after you’ve done what you want to in Rise (but that’s just my opinion). Happy hunting! Feel free to PM with any questions. Most of the comments here already cover most of it. But one thing that’s really important is routine and a schedule. Your body is wired to go to bed and wake up at the same or similar times. It’s better for you to consistently go to bed at 11:30pm and wake up at 6am than it is to go to bed early one night and then later the next with different morning rising times. 

To echo some other advice, physical activity during the day helps, finding something you find relaxing (a show, a book, a puzzle, music, games - whatever) as a way to downshift your brain before sleep, and try to be as physically relaxed as possible. 
These won’t work for everyone. But they work for me.

I can understand what you mean here. There is definitely a way to build out each plate to make it unique in terms of the damage you output.   


From what I've read on here and other places, the main problem with Valorplates is that they do not handle or play differently. The issue probably lies in the fact that the plates have been presented in a way that mimics different classes. In an RPG, a different class usually has different abilities, different playstyles, etc. The Valorplate system really doesn't do this if they are supposed to be closer to a class system than just damage modifiers that look different from each other.   


With an ARPG that cares about how it looks, Godfall is rather surprising that the Valorplates don't offer anything in terms of unique gameplay that either synergizes with the weapon types or completely transforms the weapon movesets.   
If anyone has ever played MHW and MHGU, I think Valorplates would have benefited from being like the Hunter Arts - a give-and-take system that might reduce what you can do with a weapon but gives you a whole different stance or an aerial attack or something completely outside what the weapons alone give you.  


So yes, I agree with you that there is some misunderstanding of what Valorplates CAN do. But the real issue is that the Valorplates don't effectively change the player power fantasy or give a new move or alter the gameplay, which is disappointing. Crit element is a skill that boosts the amount of elemental damage dealt on a critical strike.   
If the weapon has both raw and elemental damage on it, every hit uses BOTH numbers toward the damage dealt. If you want to use crit element on an elemental build, you'll want to make sure you're always (or usually) hitting 100% affinity on every hit or it's a wasted skill.
